fix: '<shape> at the base' (rounded to subcordate at the base) is a shape of the base of the part: the position slot must be the base, or the bearer the base of the part. A whole leaflet is not heart-shaped.
reason: The flora says the leaflets are 'rounded to slightly subcordate at the base'. Without the base, the annotation says the whole leaflet is heart-shaped, which is false (the leaflets are oblate, obovate, rhomboid or ovate).
'stipules ... adnate to petiole' gives stipule adnate towards petiole.

fix: 'transverse veins' are cross-veins (tertiary leaf vein PO_0008021). The more specific bearer is better, but vascular bundle is not false.
reason: The transverse veins of the leaf blade are undulate. 'Vascular bundle' is a broader class of the same part.
'Herbs ... unarmed' means the plant is not spiny.
'petals ... shorter than the sepals'.
'Racemes ... loosely many flowered' means many flowers in the inflorescence.
'middle pinnae 8-10 × 1.2-1.5 cm' gives a length of 8-10 cm for the median pinnae (leaflet with the median context).
In '2-8 × 2-6 cm' the second range is the blade width.

fix: In moss leaf descriptions, 'apex ..., not fragile' after the apex shape speaks of the apex: fragile leaf apices that break off are a diagnostic character.
reason: 'apex broadly acute to obtuse or rounded, often in same collection, not fragile' is said of the leaf apex, not the whole leaf.
'Herbs annual or perennial' gives life span annual or perennial.
'calyx 17-20 mm. long, hairy'.

fix: 'X or Y when young' attaches 'when young' most naturally to Y. The young stage could be added to the puberulent value, but the alternative stays true without it.
reason: The branches are glabrous or minutely puberulent. The two values as alternatives are what the flora says.
'calyx cleft ..., the lobes ... shorter than the petals': the calyx lobes (sepals) are shorter than the petals.
'Plants (3-)5-35 dm' converts to 50-350 cm, with an extreme minimum of 30 cm, as the plant height.
'Seeds 1-3' (per capsule).
'Leaves ... more or less sessile'.
'leaf blade ... adaxially glabrous' gives the adaxial leaf blade surface glabrous.
'Corolla ... limb 5-lobed' gives 5 corolla lobes.
'Umbels 2.5–6 cm across' gives an inflorescence diameter of 2.5-6 cm.
'capsule broadly ellipsoid' gives an ellipsoid fruit ('ellipsoid' is a synonym of elliptic in the lexicon).
'blades ... apex ... tapering' gives a tapered leaf lamina tip.
'étamines inégalement soudées à la base ... en un tube' means the stamens are connate (at the base). The annotation stays true without the position.
'Ripe fruit usually dull orangey brown' gives a mature fruit, usually brown.
'Capsules ovoid-obovoid' is a shape range from ovoid to obovoid.
'Inflorescences ... many-flowered'.
In botany 'strict' means straight and upright, so the scape bracts are erect.
'Stems ... ± scabrous' gives stem texture scabrous, approximately.

fix: 'heads' in Asteraceae are capitula; inflorescence is the broader but not false bearer.
reason: 'heads numerous' means many flower heads.
'Styles 3'.

fix: In 'bract-cup ... notched between acute apices and ± prominent midribs' the midribs belong to the bracts forming the cup. 'midrib' there must not fall back to leaf, and the quality belongs to the midrib, not its organ.
reason: The prominent midribs are those of the bract-cup lobes in a Euphorbiaceae cyathium, not a leaf, and the leaf itself is not called prominent.
